subject: ventures/gig-driver-earnings-report-analyzer
professional: a gig-economy tax preparer (EA/CPA) who reviews drivers' trip logs and mileage

evidence.correctness: Ran a harness (scratchpad t.mjs) on hand-computable files: net 6.6, 7.92/hr, 0.44/mi match python arithmetic; extra-miles cost 6.00, km 6.21371, dmy and midnight spans right. Two input-handling failures found (see defects); arithmetic itself held. IRS rates only cross-checked against the sibling venture, not fetched.
evidence.completeness: node --test '*.test.mjs' ran 33 pass 0 fail. Checked claimed total-row skipping, negative rows, UTF-16, km, dmy, Total-only splitting: all worked. Claimed time-of-day results fail for the common separate Date and Time column layout. Stage is prototype, no real export tested (VENTURE.yaml admits this).
evidence.verification: 33 tests pass. Four seeded mutations: extra-miles factor, daypart boundary and PM conversion caught; MIN_TRIPS 5->2 survived (ranking threshold untested). No test covers separate Date/Time columns or semicolon-with-dot decimals.
evidence.craft: Read calc.mjs (pure functions, no DOM) and page tests. Clean, but silent fallbacks: unreadable miles/minutes become null, bad tip becomes 0, decimalComma is inferred from the delimiter. README test command is bare 'node --test'.
evidence.claims: Loaded https://marisstella.app/gig-driver-earnings-report-analyzer/ (200, canonical correct); served llms.txt has marisstella.app, so the github.io host in source llms.txt is source-only. Privacy and disclaimer claims backed by page.test.mjs. Limits and not-modelled list present on page.
evidence.fitness: A driver with a one-file export with Date incl. time, Earnings, Miles, Minutes finishes the job; a driver whose export splits Date and Time loses time-of-day output silently; a dot-decimal semicolon file gives 100x pay. No real app export was ever used.
evidence.domain: Compared against IRS standard mileage rate practice and gig tax-prep habit: using the standard rate as vehicle cost is a stated proxy; per-trip miles exclude deadhead except via the extra percent; no SE tax or deduction view, and said so.

checks.what: Two-trip file net, cost, net/hr, net/mile at $0.76/mi
Vehicle cost with 20% unpaid miles and online hours: 10 mi at $0.50
Day-first dates 13/09/2026 and 02/09/2026 in one file
Semicolon file with dot decimals (12.50, 3.2) as the page reads it (decimalComma true for ';')
checks.method: plain reading of the number; node t2.mjs mirrors index.html:151

checks.what: Separate Date and Time columns, Time 18:30
checks.method: the common export shape; README says a time enables time-of-day results

checks.what: IRS mileage rate default 0.76 from 2026-07-01, 0.725 before, 0.70 for 2025
checks.method: IRS notices cited in README (Notice 2026-10); not fetched here, matches sibling venture calc.mjs written in this repo
checks.observed: matches sibling; no independent IRS fetch

checks.method: code comment says two parts read as h:mm; mm:ss is common in app exports

checks.what: Claimed: negative adjustment row and Total row handled
checks.expected: total row skipped with reason, -3.5 kept

checks.what: Served page loads and canonical points at marisstella.app
Served llms.txt has the marisstella.app host (source says github.io)
checks.method: curl served llms.txt; build rewrites hosts
page.test.mjs asserts no fetch/XHR/sendBeacon in index.html

checks.what: IRS standard rate as per-mile cost, with extra-unpaid-miles percent
checks.method: IRS standard mileage rate covers fixed and variable costs (Notice 2026-10 as cited); gig-driver tax practice uses it for deduction, not out-of-pocket cost
checks.expected: stated as proxy with advice to use own cost

defects.what: A semicolon-delimited file with dot decimals is read as decimal-comma: 12.50 becomes 1250 and 3.2 miles becomes 32, no warning
Separate Date and Time columns: the 'time' header is only an alias of the date field, so the time column is ignored and time-of-day results are dropped silently
MIN_TRIPS threshold for ranking groups is untested: changing 5 to 2 leaves all 33 tests green
Two-part durations such as 12:40 are read as h:mm (760 min) though app exports often use mm:ss
README says 'Tests: node --test', which Node 22 rejects; the glob form is needed
Source llms.txt links the github.io host; the build rewrites it and the served file is correct

verdict: Arithmetic is right: hand-computed net, per-hour, per-mile, extra-miles cost, km and day-first parsing all matched, and the served page matches its claims. It is held to prototype by input handling: a separate Time column is ignored and a semicolon file with dot decimals is silently read 100x, and one of four seeded mutations (the ranking threshold) survived. It meets the bar on the computed gates but fitness is 2 because no real export was ever used.
